findings.claim: Original 004AE000 dispatches a VLOC type-0x28 record via jump table 004AE2B4 and, conditioned on world status +0x10 bit 0x10, stores a created class-0x28 child pointer into vehicle runtime+0x398 at 004AE2A2; original 00458BF0 predicate and 004B47C0 wrapper execute, but underlying child allocation and class-runtime binding were isolated stubs.
findings.limitations: Native within a controlled synthetic class-1 root and runtime, without actual VCF loader entry; 0045EBD0 allocator and 00461970 binder intercepted; full object hierarchy/teardown not validated.

findings.claim: Retail GTSi valeprec.vdf and bus vxbus.vdf each contain a 60-byte VLOC chunk of type 0x28 at file offset 0x10A; their five VLOC type sequences are 28,2A,23,24,26 (hex), providing actual records required for the conditional camera attachment.
findings.limitations: Counts derived from exactly two byte-verified retail VDF files, not complete stock corpus; resource bytes remain private.

findings.claim: For both GTSi and bus VLOC records, executing original 00406AB0 with runtime+0x398 null follows its early return at 00406DF4, whereas after native 004AE000 stores the attachment it reaches post-guard instruction 00406B13.
findings.limitations: The original camera callback was deliberately stopped at its guard; no complete original view/projection output, runtime camera mode selection or x87 correctness was tested.

findings.claim: The writer of object status bit 0x10, runtime timing of conditional VLOC parse, child ownership and full default camera update in actual registered retail vehicle execution remain unresolved.
findings.limitations: Cannot conclude bit 0x10 always denotes the player or that a stock normal VCF construction without it should set runtime+0x398.
